name: China economy
summary: China's factory activity back in contraction in October (PMI 49.3); Q3 GDP +4.5%
state: The official NBS manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 (released 31 Oct), returning to contraction; Chinese media reported on 2 Nov that the central bank and securities regulator would meet financial institutions on supporting the capital market (AP). Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion.
for_you: China is not currently a source of global shock, though weak domestic demand keeps it reliant on exports and trade relations.
rubric_hit: Growth near target (Q3 +4.5%); no contagion; PMI dip alone not Watch

sources.title: Trading Economics — China NBS manufacturing PMI
AP — Global shares mixed and US futures advance, while oil prices fall

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
